name: Oregon Electric Railway
description: Oregon Electric Railway began as a Willamette Valley electric interurban and became an SP&S-system freight railroad, converting to diesel operation in 1945. Its operations came under Burlington Northern control in 1970, while its corporate entity continued as a BN subsidiary.

statistics.intro: Two snapshots compare the arrival of series-production diesels with the eve of Burlington Northern. Values marked ~ are project estimates; late-period equipment figures represent operation, not ownership.

routeMiles.label: Route miles
routeMiles.note: GN 1945 annual report: 202.02 miles of road operated.

employees.note: Project estimate: 202 route miles × ~1.75 employees per mile ≈ 354, rounded.

locomotives.note: Four OE ALCO RS-1s, Nos. 52–55, with possible additional SP&S power; + indicates an open-ended operated count.

rollingStock.note: Circa-1940 roster: 25 freight cars + 14 work cars + 5 cabooses + 3 motor freight cars = 47, rounded; historical comparison, not an exact 1945 count.

capitalization.note: Project estimate: ~$2.53M capital stock + ~$1.075M estimated bonds, rounded.

snapshots.label: Eve of Burlington Northern
snapshots.date: 1969 · mileage and capitalization comparison from the 1970 R-1

routeMiles.label: Route miles
routeMiles.note: Oregon Electric Railway Company 1970 R-1, Schedule 531 (printed p. 508; PDF p. 109), directly reports average mileage of road operated as 186. This is the nearest documented late-period figure used for the 1969 snapshot, not a separately verified 1969 total.

employees.note: Project estimate; no usable average-employee count was found in the 1970 R-1. Schedule 561C reports compensation applicable to prior years, not average employment.

locomotives.note: Operating-equivalent project estimate of SP&S-supplied motive power, not an OE-owned fleet total.

rollingStock.note: Operating-equivalent project estimate including SP&S-supplied equipment, not an OE-owned car total.

capitalization.note: 1970 comparison: Schedule 228 (printed p. 245; PDF p. 58) reports $2,530,000 issued stock ($1,950,000 common + $200,000 preferred + $380,000 deferred). Schedule 218 (printed pp. 234–237) reports no funded debt. Schedule 200L (printed p. 201; PDF p. 14) also shows $2,530,000 stock at March 1 and year-end 1970. This is stock plus funded debt, not total equity, authorized stock or a verified 1969 balance-sheet total.

notes: All values marked ~ are project estimates or historical proxies, not exact same-year observations.
The 1969 locomotive and rolling-stock figures are operating equivalents. SP&S supplied equipment; lack of separate OE ownership does not imply zero equipment operated.

Capitalization uses capital stock plus funded debt, not market capitalization or total shareholders’ equity. The late snapshot uses the directly reported 1970 stock and no funded debt; the report covers March 1–December 31, 1970. Mileage likewise uses the 1970 year-end comparison; employment remains a project estimate.

history: Founded in 1906, Oregon Electric linked Portland, Salem, Eugene, Corvallis/Albany and Forest Grove as an electric interurban in Oregon’s Willamette Valley. It came under Hill/SP&S control; passenger service ended in 1933 as freight became dominant.

Electric freight operation ended in 1945, when OE received four ALCO RS-1s, Nos. 52–55. These locomotives transferred to the SP&S roster in 1951; OE remained a separate corporate railroad using SP&S motive power and equipment.

OE ceased separate railroad-employer status on March 3, 1970, when its operations came under Burlington Northern control. The Oregon Electric corporate entity continued afterward as a BN-system subsidiary.
paintSchemesIntro: Oregon Electric's four ALCO RS-1s Nos. 52–55, delivered in 1945, used the contemporary SP&S G-1 green-and-yellow road-switcher scheme with OREGON ELECTRIC lettering. After their 1951 transfer to SP&S, motive power used on Oregon Electric followed SP&S paint practice.
